answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 5% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the lagoon fee is applied at the echo exit, the marble audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 28 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
